claims.text: Formation and retention of a protective oxide layer in high-temperature HEAs is governed by in situ growth of a CrTaO4-based oxide layer.
A CrTaO4-based oxide layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Blocking oxygen diffusion with the CrTaO4-based layer reduces the oxidation rate.
The proposed initial HEA systems are CrMnFeCoNi or VZrHfNbTa.
Exposure at approximately 1000°C in oxygen will induce formation of the proposed oxide layer.
In situ X-ray diffraction can monitor formation and evolution of the proposed oxide layer.
The protective structural mediator is a CrTaO4-based oxide layer.
CrTaO4 forms through reaction of Cr and Ta with oxygen.
The growth of the CrTaO4-based layer is influenced by HEA composition and microstructure.
Reduced oxygen diffusion through the oxide layer improves oxidation resistance.
Growth of a CrTaO4-based layer will produce a lower oxidation rate than in HEAs lacking a protective layer.
Formation of the CrTaO4-based layer will increase service lifetime in high-temperature environments.
The proposed mechanism applies under high-temperature, oxygen-rich conditions, exemplified by 1000°C.

contradictions.description: Neither proposed initial alloy contains both elements required for CrTaO4: CrMnFeCoNi contains Cr but no Ta, while VZrHfNbTa contains Ta but no Cr. The stated mediator therefore cannot form from either listed composition without an unstated source or compositional modification.
